subject.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution

question: Should omitted cron delivery be defaulted inside `CronService.add` for direct and declarative `current` or `session:*` callers, or must every supported caller normalize before entering the service?
rationale: Either choice affects persisted delivery behavior and caller contracts; the current patch leaves two policy owners, while recent history does not conclusively establish the permanent creation boundary.

options.title: Centralize shared creation policy
options.body: Keep the intended behavior but move the target/default decision into one helper reused by normalized and direct-service creation, with exact-head proof for both paths.

options.title: Require normalized service inputs
options.body: Keep defaulting in `normalizeCronJobCreate`, remove service-layer inference, and migrate every direct or declarative caller through normalization before persistence.

options.title: Pause the expansion
options.body: Retain isolated-only service defaulting until the cron contract owner defines and tests the direct-caller contract separately.

recommendation.title: Centralize shared creation policy
recommendation.body: Keep the intended behavior but move the target/default decision into one helper reused by normalized and direct-service creation, with exact-head proof for both paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent merged cron session-target contract and landing approval are recorded in their work on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98947.
